title: Deccan Heritage: Bijapur, Bidar, Gulbarga and Golconda
seoTitle: Deccan Sultanate Heritage: Bidar, Bijapur & Golconda | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: The monuments of the Bahmani and Deccan sultanates: Gulbarga, Bidar, Bijapur's Gol Gumbaz, Golconda, the Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar, with a route and tips.
description: A guide to the monuments of the Bahmani and Deccan sultanates: the forts and mosques of Kalaburagi (Gulbarga), Bidar's fort, madrasa and Bahmani tombs, Bijapur's Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza, Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar in Hyderabad, and Ahmednagar, with a road-trip route and tips.
dek: Between the 14th and 17th centuries, the sultanates of the Deccan built a distinctive architecture of great domes, citadels and tombs. It is still one of India's least crowded heritage trails.

hero.alt: Gol Gumbaz, the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, at Vijayapura

intro: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in the Deccan in 1347, first ruling from Gulbarga (now Kalaburagi) and later from Bidar. By the early 16th century it had broken into five successor states: the Adil Shahis of Bijapur, the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the Nizam Shahis of Ahmednagar, the Barid Shahis of Bidar and the Imad Shahis of Berar.

Their builders mixed Persian, Turkish and local Deccan traditions into a style of their own. The Monuments and Forts of the Deccan Sultanate are on India's Tentative List for UNESCO. Hyderabad is well visited, but Bidar, Kalaburagi and Bijapur are still quiet.
quickAnswer: The Deccan sultanate monuments include the fort and Jama Masjid at Kalaburagi (Gulbarga), Bidar Fort, the Mahmud Gawan madrasa and the Bahmani tombs at Ashtur, Bijapur's Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza, and Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar in Hyderabad. A six-to-eight-day road trip from Hyderabad covers them. October to February is the best time.
takeaways: The Bahmani Sultanate ruled from Gulbarga and then Bidar; five sultanates followed it.
Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur (Vijayapura) is famous for its huge dome and whispering gallery.
Hyderabad's Golconda, Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar are the easiest to reach.
The monuments are on India's UNESCO Tentative List.
Winter is the only comfortable season; the plateau is very hot from March.

rows: Mosque roofed with domes over the whole prayer hall

items.name: Golconda Fort
body: A citadel on a granite hill, famous for acoustics that carry a clap from the entrance to the top, and for the diamond trade of its region.

image.alt: The ramparts of Golconda Fort, Hyderabad
image.caption: Golconda Fort

items.name: Qutb Shahi tombs
body: The tombs of the Golconda kings, with onion domes on high platforms, restored and landscaped in recent years.

image.alt: Domed Qutb Shahi tombs near Golconda
image.caption: Qutb Shahi tombs

items.name: Charminar
body: Built in 1591 at the centre of the new city of Hyderabad, with the Mecca Masjid and Laad Bazaar around it.

items.name: Bidar
body: The fort's palaces, the ruined Mahmud Gawan madrasa with its fragments of blue tile, and the Bahmani tombs at Ashtur. Bidar is also known for Bidriware, metal inlaid with silver.

items.name: Kalaburagi (Gulbarga)
body: The early Bahmani capital, with a fort and a Jama Masjid unusual in India for being roofed over entirely by domes. The Khwaja Bande Nawaz dargah is an important Sufi shrine.

items.name: Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza
body: The tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, completed in 1656, with a vast dome and a gallery where whispers carry across the space; and Ibrahim Rauza, a tomb and mosque often admired for its proportions and carving.

sections.heading: A Deccan road trip

rows: Hyderabad: Golconda, Qutb Shahi tombs, Charminar, Chowmahalla
Vijayapura: Gol Gumbaz, Ibrahim Rauza, citadel
On to Badami and Hampi, or back to Hyderabad

after: Hyderabad has the only big airport; the rest of the route is best by car.

sections.heading: What makes the style
list: Very large domes, often on bulbous, petalled bases.
Tall, slender minarets rising from the corners of tombs.
Glazed tiles and painted plaster, particularly at Bidar.
Fortified citadels and palaces built on the plateau's granite.

sections.heading: Crafts and food
paras: The region's living heritage is as rich as its monuments. Bidriware, blackened metal inlaid with silver, is still made in Bidar. Hyderabad is known for its biryani, haleem during Ramzan and the bangles of Laad Bazaar near Charminar, and Deccani Urdu poetry and music grew up in these courts.

safety: Timings, closures and tickets change; check official sources before you go.
Start early; the Deccan plateau is hot even in winter afternoons.
Dress modestly at mosques and dargahs, and ask before photographing people at prayer.

faqs.a: The five states that followed the Bahmani Sultanate: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar and Berar.

faqs.q: What is special about Gol Gumbaz?
faqs.a: Its very large dome and the whispering gallery, where sounds carry across the space.

faqs.q: Are the Deccan sultanate monuments UNESCO sites?
faqs.a: They are on India's Tentative List, not yet inscribed.

faqs.q: How do I visit Bidar and Bijapur?
faqs.a: By road from Hyderabad; Bidar is about 145 km and Bijapur about 380 km away.
